source.pbp: NBA 2023-24 pbp (Oct-Nov 2023, 103 games / 334-game possession table), ramirobentes/nba_pbp_data

laws.statement: Defense tightens as the shot clock runs down. Nearest-defender-to-handler distance must decrease monotonically across shot-clock phases (24-18 → 18-12 → 12-6 → 6-0).
laws.metric: median nearest-defender distance to handler, per shot-clock phase
laws.tolerance: each phase median within [real*0.5, real*2.0] AND monotone or flat-within-1.5ft across phases; the 24-18 phase median must exceed the 12-6 phase median by >= 1.0ft (transition exists)

laws.statement: Off-ball players are never statues: in set offense their speed distribution is continuous with substantial mass between 1 and 7 ft/s (jog/float/relocate), not a frozen-or-sprint bimodal.
laws.metric: fraction of set-offense off-ball frames with speed in [1,7] ft/s; and p25 speed

laws.statement: Set-defense movement is human: most defender frames are under 9 ft/s (p90 real = 8.8).
laws.metric: p75 and p90 of set-defense defender speed
laws.check: p75 <= 13.0 AND p90 <= 16.0 (band allows sim discretization; real values are the target)
laws.tolerance: drift beyond band = engine producing superhuman sustained defense

laws.statement: Halfcourt offensive spacing is wide and stable: mean pairwise distance of the 5 offenders ~25ft at every shot-clock phase.
laws.check: median >= 21.0 in every phase with n >= 200 samples

laws.statement: Paint collapses draw measured help, not the whole team: when the handler is in the paint, defenders within 15ft of the rim are 1-3 (median 2), not 4-5.
laws.metric: median count of defenders within 15ft of rim during handler paint frames
laws.tolerance: weak side must keep at least one defender out of the collapse

laws.statement: Attack timing is multi-modal: terminal actions occur at every shot-clock phase (early offense exists, late bailouts exist), not one funnel.
laws.check: no phase share < 0.08 AND no phase share > 0.45 (real spread is 23-27% per phase)
laws.tolerance: note: phase label here = elapsed-since-possession-start for real data, remaining-shot-clock for sim — both measure the same thing on a 24s clock

laws.statement: Stoppage has weight: dead segments (score -> next live) exist without locking up live flow.

real.note: real make -> first offensive action includes live advance; dead-only window is brief for made baskets and longer for whistles

laws.statement: Possession durations keep the real spread: p10 <= 6s (transition kills exist), p90 >= 18s (long sets exist).
Ball screens and drives are the bread and butter: >= 1.4 screen-set events per possession across both teams and >= 0.35 drives per possession.
laws.metric: SCREEN_SET per possession; DRIVE per possession

real.note: NBA ~50 ball screens per TEAM per game over ~99 team possessions = 0.5/team-possession, 1.0 per game possession (both teams). The earlier 1.9 baseline double-counted.

laws.tolerance: under counts means the play graph underweights PNR

laws.statement: Second actions exist: after a screen is used and the action resolves, the possession may re-screen (real NBA ~35% of possessions run 2+ ball screens).
laws.metric: share of screen possessions with 2+ SCREEN_SET
laws.check: rescreenShare >= 0.05 (engine floor while the play-graph re-screen lifecycle matures)

laws.statement: The set forms before the attack: players settle at spots (3+ mates stationary >=1s) before the first terminal action in a meaningful share of possessions.
laws.metric: organizedShare (possessions with >=1s formed set before first attack)
laws.tolerance: measured behaviorally (movement <1.5ft over 0.45s), not by flags
